work_order.root_cause: The work order used the TEXT OF A DOC COMMENT as its acceptance criterion, and left four of its six criteria with no `verify` field, so the schema's default (browser) instructed QA to verify in the running app four claims that have no browser surface at all. .sdlc/bin/lib/qa-consistency.js:186 reads an absent `verify` as anything but 'test' and rejects a criterion QA proved by citing ci - which is the only honest proof available for a reading check. I ran that gate myself against the ledger work order and it rejects FIVE criteria (AC-2, AC-3, AC-4, AC-5, AC-6), not the single AC-6 the run log printed, because the log prints only the first error. Underneath the marking mistake is a rule the work order broke: an acceptance criterion is an observable claim about the product, not a description of the fix. AC-2's own text states the rule behaviourally ('the guarantee holds for every spend row that names a currency, and it names the one class of row for which it does not') and then failed to assert it behaviourally, asserting the comment instead - so no test and no browser could discharge it, and citing ci was the only move left. The same rule-break produced the three defects this PR actually shipped, all of them comments making claims nothing checks: (1) the new test comment at test/web/pages.test.js:1269 cites pages.js:881 and :897 for the two cards.map(experimentCard) sites, but the plan computed its line numbers against main and its own comment edits above them moved both sites by six lines, so on eae9a62 the sites are 887 and 903 and 881 is `if (state === 'partial') {`; (2) the rewritten comments in src/api/routes.js and src/web/pages.js now assert as durable fact that a spend row carrying NO currency is still summed and still draws a CPL, and nothing pins that - the existing leniency case (test/domain/measurement.test.js, the 'excludes foreign-currency spend rows' test) exercises a currency-less row only against a valid 'INR' tenant, and the ZZZ sweep fixture creates no spend rows at all; (3) found here and named by no prior review, the money() comment in src/web/pages.js cites the four cases that pin its 'INR' fallback by ORDINAL (15, 52, 53, 55), and an ordinal moves whenever a test is added above it - on main those same four tests are 17, 57, 58 and 60, so the shipped comment already misdirects a reader on the default branch. A comment that points at something that moved is the exact defect class issue #72 exists to remove, and this PR added three of them while removing others.
work_order.understanding: The previous work order's technical diagnosis was RIGHT and its acceptance contract was WRONG, and the second half is what sent this back twice. I re-verified the code claims line by line against eae9a62 rather than trusting them, and they all hold: the sweep is genuinely non-vacuous on /experiments, the three narrowed comments genuinely describe the code, and the implementation is correct - 64 pass / 0 fail in test/web/pages.test.js, and the caps mutation still reds 38, 45, 53, 56, 57 with the sweep among them. So no implementation work needs redoing and no root-cause diagnosis needs rewriting. WHAT WAS WRONG: the work order accepted on comment text. AC-2, AC-3 and AC-5 read as 'read the comment and confirm it says X' and AC-6 as a byte-identity check. This change edits comments and tests and moves no page, route or user-visible state, so none of the four has a browser surface. The plan gave AC-1 `verify: "test"` and left the other five unset, the schema default applied, QA - which cannot produce in-app proof for a comment and knows it - cited ci, and the gate refused, correctly. I ran the gate against the ledger work order and reproduced it exactly, and it is five criteria wide rather than the one the run log shows. I also reject the triage's proposed repair, which was to add `verify: "test"` to those criteria: it turns the gate green while leaving four criteria no test can discharge, which is a criterion laundered past the check rather than fixed. Restating each as the product claim it already names is cheap and marking them would not be, which is why the restatement is the fix. This is the 'criterion is what is wrong' case, and I can justify it without referring to the implementation at all: AC-2's own stated rule is behavioural, and the criterion asserted the comment rather than the rule. BEYOND THE MARKING: the failed run also left three real defects on the branch, all confirmed by reading the files. The stale file:line citation (test/web/pages.test.js names pages.js:881/897; the sites are 887/903 and 881 is a different statement) is a comment sending the next reader to the wrong line - the exact class this ticket exists to remove. The unpinned leniency is more load-bearing: the rewritten comments now promise in writing that a currency-less spend row is still summed and still draws a CPL, and I confirmed that is true end-to-end (live ingest, ZZZ tenant, spend_micros 5000000, a real CPL, a rupee tile on the dashboard) and that nothing pins it. A comment asserting a behaviour nothing checks is how the original overstatement happened, one release later. The third, which I found here, is the same class as the second: the money() comment names its four covering cases by ordinal, and those ordinals are already wrong on main. Two things I checked and found need NO work, which is why the file list is three test files and one comment rather than the previous revision's five: the routes.js and pages.js comments ALREADY name computeFunnel and normaliseGrowthEvent for the lines they cite, so the previous revision's proposed src edits were no-ops; and every restated criterion's underlying claim already holds in code. I answer the three plan-reviewer objections on the refused revision explicitly: the counts are recomputed as 66 / 308 / 48 and every one of them is pinned to its base commit alongside the four test names, so the number and the list cannot disagree in one sentence; the citation guard is specified ONE way - option (b), parsed citations, with the line number read out of the comment and never hardcoded, which is the version AC-8's own check text describes; and no acceptance criterion names a line number as its verification step, because the branch is three commits behind main and main's pages.js has the money() fallback at 354 and the two cards.map sites at 977/993. validated_work_order.root_cause: The citation guard in test/web/pages.test.js is a hand-maintained table of claims with four independent blind spots, and between them they account for every citation QA and I have found going stale. (1) EXPRESSION SETS CANNOT EXPRESS POSITION. Each entry declares `expressions`, a set of distinct strings, and asserts every captured citation lands on a line holding one of them, then that every expression is held by some citation. The override-loop comment names TWO sites that hold the IDENTICAL text, so the entry declares one expression - and one citation then satisfies direction two for both sites. The comment writes the first number as 'pages.js:988' and the second bare, as '1004 for the ideal page'; the extractor is `new RegExp(basename + ':(\d+)', 'g')`, so only the first is a citation by the guard's own grammar. Move the ideal-page site off 1004 and the comment's second location is not merely unchecked, it is not even parsed: 74/74 green while a reader following it lands on a blank line. Move 988 instead and it reds instantly, on one character of formatting. That is BUG-1. (2) NOTHING CHECKS THE TABLE'S COVERAGE. The only completeness assertion is `citations.length > 0` per entry - that the entry guards SOMETHING, never that it guards EVERY citation the branch wrote. The branch added five file:line citations across five reader files; the table covered three pairs. test/api/events.test.js:496 and test/domain/measurement.test.js:363 named no entry, so either could be rewritten to point at any line in the repository - I set them to measurement.js:999 and measurement.js:888, both of which hold nothing of the kind, and the full 475-test suite stayed green. That is BUG-1 with the guard deleted, and it is the half that actually costs the guarantee. (3) A CLAIMED PAIR IS NOT A COVERED PAIR, WHICH IS WHAT THE PLAN REVIEWER MEASURED. The one entry for (test/web/pages.test.js, src/web/pages.js) is anchor-scoped to the 'cards.map(experimentCard) branches' comment, so the per-entry loop never reads the other comment in that same reader that cites the same file - the pendingApprovalRepos note at test/web/pages.test.js:90. Editing src/web/pages.js:924, the line that citation names, leaves the file at 74/0. Any pair-level coverage check reports that pair as covered, because the pair IS claimed, and the citation inside it is therefore declared guarded and then never resolved. This is the same defect class as (2) wearing a different hat: the mechanism asserts what it was told about, never that it was told everything, and 'this entry has an anchor' reads as coverage when it is the opposite. The comment behind that citation is not merely stale, it is false - it claims a grep hit for approval.requested at a line that is `function experimentCard`, and approval.requested does not occur anywhere in src/. (4) THEREFORE NO FUTURE CITATION IS GUARDED BY DEFAULT. A hand-maintained table falls behind the comments it polices and nothing in the suite notices on the change that lets it. The design consequence is the same in all four: the guard asserts that what it was told about is true, and never that it was told everything.
